title_en: New ETFs to Watch: A $2.5 Billion Launch, Anthropic and S&P 10,000, Anyone?
title_zh: 值得关注的新 ETF：25 亿美元的巨无霸发行、Anthropic，还有谁想赌 S&P 涨到 10,000 点？
subtitle_zh: 本期“值得关注的新 ETF”盘点了三款产品：一只由 University of California 捐赠基金注资 25 亿美元的 SPDR 90/10 组合、Roundhill 那只押注 S&P 500 涨到 10,000 点、代码叫 XX 的高投机产品，以及欧洲一只用 ETF 外壳提供 Anthropic 敞口的合成型 ETP。Eric Balchunas、Joel Weber 和市场线记者 Isabel Lee 一起，聊聊这些新品的看点，也少不了几段“祝你好运”时刻。
description: New ETFs to Watch: A $2.5 Billion Launch, Anthropic and S&P 10,000, Anyone?

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios, podcasts, radio, news. Buffett, when he, Berkshire shareholders would ask him what to invest in. And he said, look, if you're not monitoring the markets all day, the best thing would be what I'm doing in my will, which is I said to my wife and my trust that you should put 90% in an index fund, preferably Vanguard is what he said, and 10% in like short-term treasuries. And so I call that the Buffett special. Welcome to Trillions.
turns.zh: Bloomberg Audio Studios，播客、广播、新闻。当年 Berkshire 的股东问 Buffett 该投资什么，他说：听着，如果你没法整天盯着市场，最好的做法就是我在遗嘱里安排的那样——我跟我妻子和我的信托说，把 90% 放进一只指数基金（index fund），最好是 Vanguard，这是他的原话；另外 10% 放进短期国债（short-term Treasuries）之类的。所以我把这个叫作“Buffett 特餐”。欢迎收听 Trillions。

turns.en: I'm Joel Weber.
turns.zh: 我是 Joel Weber。

turns.en: And I'm Eric Balchunas.
turns.zh: 我是 Eric Balchunas。

turns.en: It's time for our monthly new ETFs to watch episode. Our big hit is a whale that Warren Buffett is going to love. Our wild card is a delightfully weird, highly speculative product with a memorable ticker. And we're also going to mention a noteworthy product out of Europe that gets anthropic exposure in an ETF wrapper. And then there's our good luck with that category. Joining us, Isabel Lee, who... Has a new job at Bloomberg. Congrats, Isabel.
turns.zh: 又到了我们每月一期的“值得关注的新交易所交易基金（ETF）”环节。今天的“大热门”（big hit）是一头 Warren Buffett 一定会喜欢的“巨鲸”（whale）；“外卡”（wild card）则是一款妙趣横生、高度投机、代码过目难忘的产品。我们还会提到欧洲一款值得关注的产品，它用 ETF 的外壳让你获得 Anthropic 的敞口（exposure）。然后还有我们的“祝你好运”（good luck with that）类别。今天做客的是 Isabel Lee，她……刚在 Bloomberg 有了份新工作。恭喜啊，Isabel。

turns.en: Thank you. I'm still a markets reporter, but now I'm with the TV side. So still the same. Honored and humbled. I'm blinded. Eric is beside me. Oh my God, I'm blinded. Wearing my sunglasses. So blinded.
turns.zh: 谢谢。我还是个市场线记者，只不过现在转到了电视那边。所以还是老样子，倍感荣幸、也诚惶诚恐。我被晃瞎了，Eric 就坐在我旁边。天呐，我快瞎了，得戴上墨镜。太刺眼了。

turns.en: Well, congratulations and looking forward to having you on the podcast.
turns.zh: 恭喜恭喜，也很期待你上我们的播客。

turns.en: She's still the same Isabel, just way bigger head. Just way bigger. Yeah. That's how I see it. We knew her when.
turns.zh: 她还是原来那个 Isabel，就是脑袋大了一大圈。真的大了一大圈。对，我就是这么看的。我们可是看着她一路走过来的。

turns.en: Not bigger than Eric. So that's at least there.
turns.zh: 再大也大不过 Eric。所以这点起码还算强。

turns.en: She and I can't fit through a door together. Not because we're overweight.
turns.zh: 我和她没法一起挤过一扇门。倒不是因为我们胖。

turns.en: I don't know how we're in the studio together right now.
turns.zh: 我都不知道咱仨现在是怎么一起待在录音棚里的。

turns.en: I'm just so small in the corner.
turns.zh: 我就小小地缩在角落里。

turns.en: All right.
turns.zh: 好了。

turns.en: Let's talk about the big hit, Eric. What is it? All right. The State Street Spider UC Investments 9010 Endowment Strategy Index ETF. Is that a new record for longest title? We used to track this. I don't think this has got it because one of the ones that made it was the whole first line of the five line DES page. And this is only about 60% of it. The ticker though, UCBG. What's this thing doing?
turns.zh: 来聊聊今天的“大热门”吧，Eric，是什么？好，是 State Street 的 SPDR UC Investments 90/10 Endowment Strategy Index ETF。这会不会创了最长名字的新纪录？我们以前还专门统计过这个。我觉得它还真破不了纪录，因为当年上榜的一只，名字整整占满了那份五行 DES 页面的第一行，而这个大概只有它的 60%。不过代码是 UCBG。这东西到底是干嘛的？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Yeah. So very simple. It's 90% the S & P 500 and 10% short-dated bonds. This is something akin to what I used to call the Buffett portfolio. Because Buffett, when Berkshire shareholders would ask him what to invest in, and he said, look, if you're not monitoring the markets all day, the best thing would be what I'm doing in my will, which is I said to my wife and my trust that you should put 90% in an index fund, preferably Vanguard is what he said, and 10% in short-term treasuries. And so I called out the Buffett Special and talked about how to do it with ETFs. It's interesting that this big institution is doing it.
turns.zh: 嗯，其实很简单：90% 是 S&P 500，10% 是短期债券。这就有点像我以前说的“Buffett 组合”。因为当年 Berkshire 的股东问 Buffett 该投资什么，他说：听着，如果你没法整天盯着市场，最好的做法就是我在遗嘱里安排的那样——我跟我妻子和我的信托说，把 90% 放进一只指数基金，最好是 Vanguard，这是他的原话；另外 10% 放进短期国债。所以我当时点出了这个“Buffett 特餐”，还讲了怎么用 ETF 来实现它。有意思的是，现在这么大一家机构真在这么做。

turns.en: But even more interesting- That institution is University of California?
turns.zh: 但更有意思的是——那家机构是 University of California？

turns.en: Yeah, the investment arm of UCAL, basically. It was actually just over there in Berkeley, by the way, Joel. I visited my ex-girlfriend, but we were all part of a huge house.
turns.zh: 对，基本上就是 UC 的投资部门。顺便说一句，Joel，其实就在 Berkeley 那边。我去看我前女友，我们当时一大帮人住在一栋大房子里。

turns.en: Very mature, Eric.
turns.zh: 真成熟啊，Eric。

turns.en: It was like real world, five guys, five girls.
turns.zh: 就跟《Real World》那种设定似的，五个男生、五个女生。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: And it was- So many questions. This is what happened in the 90s.
turns.zh: 而且那——问题可太多了。这都是 90 年代发生的事儿。

turns.en: So many questions.
turns.zh: 问题太多了。

turns.en: Anyway, we stayed friends and I went out to visit her and Berkeley is nice, man. I was there one summer in the 90s and it was a little more like gutter punks and hippies. It's got a little of that still, but it's way richer. Anyhow, UC Berkeley is the college there. Everybody's trying to get in. It's hard to get in. It's hard to get in. It's hard to get in anywhere these days, by the way.
turns.zh: 总之我们后来一直还是朋友，我去找她玩，Berkeley 真挺不错的。90 年代有一个夏天我在那儿待过，那时候更多是些街头朋克和嬉皮士。现在还有点那种味道，但明显富裕多了。反正 UC Berkeley 就是那儿的大学，人人都想挤进去，很难进。真的很难进。顺便说一句，如今哪儿都很难进。

turns.en: This is a straightforward rules-based asset allocation and it's very cheap. It's like six basis points. But, I mean, it's just one fund so far. I mean, so then for me, okay, congratulations. Successful. Two and a half billion dollars AUM.
turns.zh: 这是一个简单直接、基于规则（rules-based）的资产配置，而且非常便宜，大概 6 个基点（basis points）。但我是说，目前也就只有这一只基金。所以对我来说，好吧，恭喜，很成功——25 亿美元的资产管理规模（AUM）。

turns.en: Well, that's the big, that's a lot of money.
turns.zh: 哇，那可是……那可是好大一笔钱。

turns.en: I know, but so then.
turns.zh: 我知道，但话又说回来。

turns.en: So this is like, to have an endowment have two and a half billion dollars as a seed.
turns.zh: 所以说，这相当于一家捐赠基金（endowment）拿出 25 亿美元作为种子资金（seed）。

turns.en: Has there ever been that much money seeded? Close. iShares and Xtrackers both had European pensions, I believe, seed ESG funds with about $ 2 billion. So this is up there. This might be a little bigger. And anyway, if you're going to get a whale, you take it.
turns.zh: 以前有过这么多钱的种子资金吗？接近。我记得 iShares 和 Xtrackers 都曾有欧洲的养老金为它们的 ESG 基金注资大约 20 亿美元。所以这个也算排得上号了，说不定还更大一点。总之，你要是能钓到一头巨鲸，那就笑纳呗。

turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: Because then there's no more pressure. If the little minnows come in, fine, but I'm going to eat for a while because $ 2 billion on even six bips is going to make it probably profitable.
turns.zh: 因为这样一来就没压力了。要是有些小鱼小虾再进来，那也行，但我已经能撑上一阵子了——毕竟 20 亿美元哪怕只按 6 个基点收费，也基本上能让它盈利了。

turns.en: So I guess my question was, should they work hard to get another whale? Or you're saying that, no, they could just coast for a while with this one huge giant whale.
turns.zh: 所以我想问的是，他们该不该再努力去拉来另一头巨鲸？还是说，就像你说的，不用，靠这一头巨大的鲸鱼就能悠哉悠哉地过一阵子。

turns.en: Yeah, this is going to be tricky because... It's 90-10, and I guess they could go out and say, well, look, this is what the institutions do. And if they're using their money in it, then you should do it too. The problem is advisors tend to want to pick the different pieces. And so this one tries to kind of do that. And most people already own the S & P 500, so they already have 90% of this covered. They probably own bonds. So this is almost redundant to what most people already own. That's the challenge here.
turns.zh: 对，这会比较棘手，因为……它是 90/10 的组合，我猜他们大可以出去宣传说：瞧，机构就是这么做的，既然他们真金白银投在里面，那你也该跟着做。问题是，投资顾问往往更想自己去挑各个部件，而这只产品想做的恰恰就是把部件打包好。可大多数人本来就持有 S&P 500，也就是说这里面 90% 的部分他们已经有了；他们大概也持有债券。所以对多数人来说，这只产品几乎跟他们已有的东西重复了。这才是难点所在。

turns.en: Who's going to buy it?
turns.zh: 那谁会买它呢？

turns.en: I don't know.
turns.zh: 我也不知道。

turns.en: I don't think hedge funds will because I think they're shunning the alternative heavy approach, right? And that's what hedge funds typically want. So they just need to capture another endowment whale.
turns.zh: 我觉得对冲基金（hedge fund）不会买，因为他们现在正回避那种另类资产占大头的路子，对吧？而那恰恰是对冲基金通常想要的。所以他们只需要再拿下另一头捐赠基金巨鲸就行了。

turns.en: Yeah, I guess so. They could probably just, yeah, shop this around to endowments who... The one thing endowments like about ETFs, they can get this strategy on a separate account, sort of like getting a tailored suit. But six bips is about as cheap as they'd get, especially mid to small ones. So I could see maybe a mid or small institution wanting to use this for their sort of beta exposure and State Street's reputable and that they like the liquidity where you can get in and out of it very quickly. I don't have to call anybody. There's no contracts. But still, even with all that, I just think it's probably going to be an uphill battle. The ESG funds that were seeded, they had the same problem. I'm yet to see a huge institution seed an ETF and it kicks off some frenzy. Usually they're very specific to the institution and they just don't catch on with the rest of the world for various reasons. One quick thing on this though, this is modeled after apparently the blue and gold endowment pool for UC. So my guess is they might want to have something that people who are in the fund can get in and out of easily. Usually when an institution does something like this, it's not because they need exposure. Again, they can get cheap exposure. It's because they want to create something for other people, maybe members or other investors who are part of the institution who can go in and out of it easily. That's the main reason they use an ETF is access, liquidity, and ease of use. Because all their other stuff is going to be in private investments, alternatives, the Yale model type stuff. And if they went into a S & P 500, they could probably get it for like two basis points from State Street themselves. So I just think this is for easy access and liquidity. Use Fisher did the same thing with those seeded ones. So that's why it's the biggest. But one investor, I guess you could say it's not organically the biggest, but it was the biggest in assets of the new crop.
turns.zh: 对，我想是的。他们大概就……yeah，把这个推销给那些捐赠基金。捐赠基金喜欢 ETF 的一点是，他们可以通过独立账户（separate account）拿到这个策略，有点像定制西装。但 6 个基点已经是他们能拿到的最低价了，尤其中小型机构是这样。所以我能想象，也许某家中小型机构会想用它来做自己的贝塔（beta）敞口，而且 State Street 声誉好，他们也喜欢那种流动性——可以非常快地进出，不用给任何人打电话，也没有合约约束。但即便如此，把这些都算上，我仍然觉得这会是一场硬仗。那些拿到种子资金的 ESG 基金也有同样的问题。我还没见过哪家巨型机构给一只 ETF 注资、然后就掀起什么狂热的。通常这些产品都非常贴合那家机构自身的需要，因为各种各样的原因，就是没法在外部世界流行起来。不过关于这个还有一点，它显然是照着 UC 的 Blue and Gold 捐赠基金池做的。所以我猜他们可能想做一个让池子里的人能够轻松进出的东西。通常一家机构做这种事，并不是因为他们自己需要敞口——再说一遍，他们能拿到很便宜的敞口——而是因为他们想为其他人做点东西，也许是机构里的成员或其他投资人，让他们能轻松进出。他们用 ETF 的主要原因就是准入、流动性和易用性。因为他们其他的钱都会放在私募投资、另类投资（alternatives）里，就是耶鲁模式（Yale model）那一类；而如果要买 S&P 500，他们直接从 State Street 自己那儿大概 2 个基点就能拿到。所以我觉得这就是为了便捷的准入和流动性。Use Fisher 当年对那些拿到种子资金的产品也是这么干的，所以它才是最大的。不过只有一个投资人，我猜你可以说它不是靠有机增长成为最大的，但它确实是这批新产品里资产规模最大的一只。

turns.en: What is the origin of this? Did UC have this idea and State Street was like, okay, let's seize the moment and launch this ETF? Or did they launch an ETF and UC was like, that is perfect?
turns.zh: 这个是怎么来的？是 UC 先有了这个想法，然后 State Street 说“好，那就趁热打铁把这只 ETF 推出来”？还是他们先做出了这只 ETF，然后 UC 说“这个太合适了”？

turns.en: It's a great question. State Street has been on a roll getting these institutions. They got Bridgewater. They got Apollo. They must have a team of people who just go and talk to institutions. Yeah. And the reason you take State Street's call to institutions, they have all the big liquid ETFs. Even though these institutions have anything they want, the world is their oyster for almost no fee. They can't get liquidity from other things. So State Street has a bunch of liquid ETFs. So they probably know State Street just from using some of their liquid ETFs for cash requisition. While they're talking, maybe State Street just offers this or maybe they bring it up and they're like, oh yeah, you want that? We can do that. Let's do it. And then all of a sudden it's a deal. So I'm yet to see these kind of deals with anybody other than like BlackRock and State Street, though. This is like a big fish type situation.
turns.zh: 这是个好问题。State Street 最近在这些机构客户身上下手很顺，拿下了 Bridgewater，也拿下了 Apollo。他们肯定有一支专门跑去跟机构谈的团队。对。机构之所以愿意接 State Street 的电话，是因为他们手里有所有那些大型、高流动性的 ETF。虽然这些机构想要什么就有什么，几乎不花什么费用就能予取予求，但别的东西给不了他们流动性。而 State Street 有一堆高流动性的 ETF，所以他们光是用 State Street 的一些流动性 ETF 来做现金调配，就已经认识这家了。聊着聊着，也许 State Street 就顺势把这个方案抛出来，或者机构自己提起来，State Street 就说“哦，你想要那个？我们能做，那就干吧”，然后一桩买卖就这么成了。不过，除了 BlackRock 和 State Street 这类玩家，我还没见过谁能做成这种交易。这属于大鱼通吃的局面。

turns.en: All right. Next up, we're going to talk wildcard, and it's not going to be about Eric's housing situation.
turns.zh: 好，接下来我们聊聊“外卡”，不过这次不讲 Eric 的住房问题了。

turns.en: When he was in the 90s.
turns.zh: 就是他 90 年代那会儿的。

turns.en: Or ex-girlfriend, anyway.
turns.zh: 或者前女友吧，反正。

turns.en: This ticker, though, is maybe the best ticker I think we've ever had on the show. XX.
turns.zh: 不过这个代码，可能是我们节目有史以来最妙的一个代码——XX。

turns.en: I didn't know that that was even an option.
turns.zh: 我都不知道原来这也能当代码。

turns.en: The Roundhill Target 10,020.
turns.zh: Roundhill Target 10,020。

turns.en: Maybe that does relate to my situation. I don't want to know. I don't want to know. Okay, so what is going on at Roundhill? It doesn't currently.
turns.zh: 说不定这还真跟我的情况有关系。我不想知道，我不想知道。好，那 Roundhill 这是在搞什么？它目前并不……

turns.en: We can talk about it after the show anyway.
turns.zh: 反正这个我们节目录完再聊。

turns.en: Okay. The ticker is kind of cool. XX, right? The Roundhill S & P 500 Target 10,020 ETF. Another mouthful. These names and ideas are getting really more elaborate every month, aren't they? Anyway.
turns.zh: 好，这代码挺酷的，XX，对吧？Roundhill S&P 500 Target 10,020 ETF，又是一个绕口的名字。这些名字和创意真的是一个月比一个月复杂，是不是？总之……

turns.en: Every day.
turns.zh: 是一天比一天复杂。

turns.en: This is an ETF designed to solve a problem with leveraged ETFs. You know how when you buy them, they reset every day and you get the corrosion? That daily resetting corrodes your returns. You can't hold it long term.
turns.zh: 这是一只专门为解决杠杆 ETF（leveraged ETF）某个问题而设计的 ETF。你知道的，你买杠杆 ETF 的时候，它们每天都会重置，于是就有了那种侵蚀（corrosion）——每日重置会一点点侵蚀你的收益，所以你没法长期持有。

turns.en: Yes. Typically. The volatility drag.
turns.zh: 对，通常就是这样，也就是波动拖累（volatility drag）。

turns.en: This is saying let's not use daily resetting and swaps. Let's just buy a long, long, long, long call dated option.
turns.zh: 而这只产品的思路是：咱们别用每日重置加掉期（swap）那一套了，直接买入一个很久、很久、很久、很久到期日的看涨期权（call option）就行。

turns.en: 2030 long.
turns.zh: 到期日到 2030 年那么久。

turns.en: It's literally in 2030. That's a long time away. So we're going to buy its options, but they're all very long dated. They buy the option and you just wait. And the idea here is if the S & P hits $ 10, 000, you're in the money. From there, you get grow and grow and grow your investment. And the ETF can be traded because the outlook of whether the S & P will hit $ 10, 000 will change. So the ETF itself might move based on the expectation. But it's an interesting way to add some leverage without having the corrosion of volatility drag. However, and I am not an expert on theta, which is this sort of time decay of options, but there is probably some theta in there, which is there is some decay, but not as bad as a leverage ETF. I put this on Twitter and it got real viral. And normally I tweet these new ETFs.
turns.zh: 它的到期日确确实实在 2030 年，那还有好长一段时间。所以我们要买它的期权，但都是到期日非常长的期权。他们买入期权，你就等着。这里的逻辑是：如果 S&P 涨到 10,000 点，你就处于价内（in the money），从那之后你的投资就会不断增长、增长、再增长。而且这只 ETF 是可以交易的，因为“S&P 能不能涨到 10,000 点”这个预期是会变化的，所以 ETF 本身的价格也会随预期波动。这是一种挺有意思的加杠杆方式，又没有波动拖累那种侵蚀。不过——我对 theta 并不在行，也就是期权那种随时间流逝的衰减（time decay）——但里面大概率是有一些 theta 的，也就是说会有一定衰减，只是没杠杆 ETF 那么糟。我把这个发到 Twitter 上，结果火得不行。要知道我平时也会发这些新 ETF。

turns.en: What were the comments?
turns.zh: 评论区都说什么了？

turns.en: Half the people were like, oh my God, this is such a great idea. Like I've wanted something like this. And then half the people were like, oh, look at this bullshit. Like this is just a dumb idea for retail investors. Like can't people calm down?
turns.zh: 一半的人说：天呐，这主意太棒了，我一直就想要这样的东西。另一半人则说：哦，看看这什么玩意儿，纯粹是坑散户的蠢主意。我就想说，大家能不能淡定点？

turns.en: It does sound like a prediction market. Let's see if it hits 10,000.
turns.zh: 它听起来确实像个预测市场（prediction market）：就看它能不能涨到 10,000 点。

turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: Yes or no.
turns.zh: 要么到，要么不到。

turns.en: I don't know how to feel about the all or nothing structure of the index.
turns.zh: 对于这个指数那种“要么全有、要么全无”的结构，我还真不知道该作何感想。

turns.en: Yeah. So what happens to my money if it doesn't hit?
turns.zh: 是啊，那如果没涨到，我的钱会怎么样？

turns.en: Yeah. Eric, tell us.
turns.zh: 对，Eric，你来说说。

turns.en: Yeah. So let's go over the scenarios here. If the S & P is at 10,000 or above, the options deliver a substantial leverage payout. I think I did the math. 10,000 is like 7% a year from here. Okay. Don't quote me on that. Something like that. That's not that extreme, but we've been up a lot. So if we go down a lot, that percent goes up a lot. But the way the market's going, it just seems so easy to achieve right now, but we're in a bull market. Now, if it underachieves that, the options expire completely worthless, meaning the fund risks losing its entire value. And what happens to your money?
turns.zh: 好，那我们来把几种情形过一遍。如果 S&P 到了 10,000 点或以上，这些期权就会给出相当可观的杠杆式回报。我记得我算过，从现在起涨到 10,000 点大概是年化 7% 左右。好，这个数字别拿去引用啊，反正差不多这个量级。这算不上多极端，但我们已经涨了很多，所以如果我们大跌，那个年化涨幅要求就会大幅上升。不过照现在市场的走势，它眼下看起来太容易实现了——当然，我们正处在牛市里。可要是没达到那个点位，期权就会彻底变成废纸，也就是说这只基金有可能亏掉全部价值。那你的钱会怎么样呢？

turns.en: It's gone too. Gone. G-O-N-E.
turns.zh: 也跟着没了。没了，G-O-N-E，彻底没了。

turns.en: Yeah, well, a call option is to buy something back at a current price. And if it doesn't hit that price, then the option expires worthless. Now, I don't know if they put some other stuff in there to maybe give you some, like, maybe they add a little something so you're not home with, like, zero. I got to look into it more. But this is, Roundhill, you got to give it up. They're pretty innovative. They had the biggest breakout hit of the year with DRAM.
turns.zh: 是啊，嗯，看涨期权就是以某个约定价格买入某样东西的权利，如果没涨到那个价格，期权就作废了。不过，我不确定他们有没有在里面放点别的，也许给你留一点什么——比如稍微加点东西，让你不至于血本无归、一分不剩。这个我得再研究研究。但说到 Roundhill，你真得服他们，相当有创新精神。他们今年最大的爆款就是 DRAM。

turns.en: DRAM.
turns.zh: DRAM。

turns.en: They've launched a bunch of other stuff. They hired the ex-strategist from Citi, Drew Pettit, who was on ETF IQ talking about this. And so look, the way it polarized people and had people reacting, I just thought it was a good wild card this week, but it doesn't have a ton of money so far. So even though it started trading, like DRAM was a hitter off the bat. This one hasn't seen much action. Maybe it will. Other people have tried monthly and even quarterly resetting leverage ETFs and nobody cares. So this might be in that bucket of like, it just has to be daily resetting and give me that juice every day or I don't care.
turns.zh: 他们还推出了一堆别的产品。他们请来了 Citi 的前策略师 Drew Pettit，他上过 ETF IQ 聊这只产品。所以你看，就凭它能把人们分成两派、引发这么大反应，我就觉得它是本周一个不错的外卡。不过到目前为止它还没吸引到太多资金。所以尽管它已经开始交易了——你看 DRAM 一上来就是爆款——这一只却没什么动静。也许会有的。别人也试过按月、甚至按季度重置的杠杆 ETF，结果没人在意。所以这只可能就属于那一类：要么就得每日重置、每天都给我来点刺激，要么我就懒得理。

turns.en: Defiance is trying for an hourly.
turns.zh: Defiance 正在尝试做按小时重置的。

turns.en: Yeah, that's even like, that's to go another way and saying, oh, you want juice?
turns.zh: 对，那个就更——那是往另一个方向走，等于在说：哦，你想要刺激是吧？

turns.en: Here's a lot of juice.
turns.zh: 来，给你一大堆刺激。

turns.en: Here's a waterfall. That probably will work. I think just generally speaking, if you increase the purity of the juice, you will get bites.
turns.zh: 给你一整道瀑布。那个大概会管用。我觉得笼统地说，只要你把这份“刺激”的纯度提上去，就会有人上钩。

turns.en: It's orange concentrate.
turns.zh: 那是橙汁浓缩液。

turns.en: It's concentration, yeah. I could totally see this, though.
turns.zh: 是浓缩的，对。不过这种我还真能想象得到。

turns.en: There are so many other versions of this of like, what's the Bitcoin version of this, right?
turns.zh: 这种东西会有很多别的版本，比如它的 Bitcoin 版本会是什么样，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: There's going to be, if this takes off.
turns.zh: 只要这个火起来，一定会有。

turns.en: If this is a hit, of course, they'll make a ton of sequels like Marvel comic movies.
turns.zh: 如果它成了爆款，那当然，他们会像 Marvel 漫画电影那样拍出一大堆续集。

turns.en: There's a thing that you do, which is we try and limit this to three ETFs and then you always have like four or five.
turns.zh: 你有个习惯，就是我们本来想把这期限制在三只 ETF，结果你总是能整出四五只来。

turns.en: Wait, I'm sorry. And I know you told me not to do this, but I just have to just crowbar this in. I want to just quickly talk about another wild card that happened in Europe. I don't tend to get it. My attention doesn't divert to Europe all that often. There's not a ton going on. 21 shares, anthropic synthetic ETP launched.
turns.zh: 等等，抱歉。我知道你跟我说过别这么干，但我就是得硬塞进来一个。我想快速聊另一只在欧洲出现的“外卡”。我平时不太关注那边，注意力不常往欧洲跑，那儿也没太多动静。21Shares 推出了一只 Anthropic 的合成型 ETP（synthetic ETP）。

turns.en: What's the ticker?
turns.zh: 代码是什么？

turns.en: C-L-A-U.
turns.zh: C-L-A-U。

turns.en: Oh, nice.
turns.zh: 哦，不错。

turns.en: Here's why this is interesting. This uses swaps that link to perpetual futures that link to reference prices for anthropic private shares. So in a way, they are, again, ipso facto through a bunch of means getting you anthropic exposure on a public market. This is the first ETF to give you 100% of a private exposure, and it's doing it for one company.
turns.zh: 有意思的地方在这儿：它用掉期挂钩永续期货（perpetual futures），而永续期货又挂钩 Anthropic 私募股份的参考价格。所以某种意义上，他们又是通过一连串手段，事实上让你在公开市场上拿到了 Anthropic 的敞口。这是第一只给你 100% 私募敞口（private exposure）的 ETF，而且它只针对一家公司。

turns.en: Expensive, though. 100 basis points.
turns.zh: 不过挺贵的，100 个基点。

turns.en: Yeah, so that would be a lot. But for the degen trading crowd, that's not a big deal. Also, for something so novel.
turns.zh: 对，那算不少了。但对那帮 degen（赌徒式）交易者来说，这不算什么。而且对这么新奇的东西来说也是如此。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: And Anthropic, I think we looked at the, we actually can price where Anthropic is from mutual fund holdings. And I believe it was up something like 150% in the past like 15 months. So you don't care about 1% if something is going up like that. Yeah, I guess so. So it's interesting to see this. Now, this is the wrong market. Europe, I just– they're so sleepy. They don't really take to hot sauce. But there's an ETF filed here by Defiance that's going to do the same thing. Swaps to perps to the ETF. And that would be the way to give you privates. Anyway, just something to be aware of.
turns.zh: 至于 Anthropic，我记得我们看过——其实我们能通过共同基金的持仓来给 Anthropic 定价。我相信它在过去大约 15 个月里涨了差不多 150%。所以如果一样东西涨成这样，你才不会在乎那 1% 的费用。是啊，我也这么想。所以看到这个挺有意思。不过，这是选错了市场。欧洲嘛，我只能说——他们太“温吞”了，接受不了辣酱。但 Defiance 已经在这边提交了一只 ETF 的申请，要做同样的事：掉期挂钩永续期货、再做成 ETF，那才是给你私募敞口的正确姿势。总之，算是个值得留意的东西。

turns.en: Does any of this matter before– it matters before an IPO?
turns.zh: 这些东西在——它在 IPO（首次公开募股）之前有意义吗？

turns.en: Does it matter after? That's a good question. Maybe they'll convert it to a 2X version of Anthropic. or you'll just keep your shares if you don't want to, like, realize capital gains.
turns.zh: 那 IPO 之后还有意义吗？这是个好问题。也许他们会把它转换成 2 倍做多的 Anthropic 版本；或者如果你不想实现资本利得（capital gains），也可以就这么一直持有你的份额。

turns.en: It reminds me of all the ETFs that said they tracked SpaceX before SpaceX went public, and that was their whole selling point. And when SpaceX went public, you know, and then the NASDAQ had SpaceX.
turns.zh: 这让我想起，在 SpaceX 上市之前，有一堆 ETF 都号称自己追踪 SpaceX，那就是它们全部的卖点。而等 SpaceX 真上市了，你知道的，然后 NASDAQ 上就有了 SpaceX。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Yeah, you know what? We should check up on what happened to those. Anyway.
turns.zh: 是啊，你知道吗？我们真该回头查查那些产品后来怎么样了。总之……

turns.en: I'm always, if you, a lot of times these ETFs launch, and if you get, like, say, $ 100 million, and then the thing that was so hot goes away, only half the people leave anyway. So, like, People just forget they buy stuff, I think. Or they don't want to take the taxes. Half the people always stay. I'm not that person.
turns.zh: 我总是觉得——很多时候这些 ETF 上市，比如募到了 1 亿美元，然后当初那个火热的题材凉了，结果也只有一半的人会走。所以，我觉得人们就是买完东西然后就忘了，或者他们不想承担那笔税。总有一半的人会一直留着。反正我不是那种人。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: Where's my money again?
turns.zh: 我的钱又跑哪儿去了？

turns.en: All right.
turns.zh: 好了。

turns.en: Good luck with that category.
turns.zh: 下面是“祝你好运”类别。

turns.en: Good luck with that. What is it, Eric?
turns.zh: “祝你好运”。是什么呀，Eric？

turns.en: What's our winner this episode?
turns.zh: 这一期我们的“赢家”是谁？

turns.en: Okay. This one is Direction US 500 Plus ETF.
turns.zh: 好，这只是 Direxion US 500 Plus ETF。

turns.en: Ticker SPXP.
turns.zh: 代码 SPXP。

turns.en: Yeah. This is kind of an- It's a baby.
turns.zh: 对，这个算是——它还是个“婴儿”。

turns.en: It launched just like- Less than two weeks ago.
turns.zh: 它上市才……不到两周。

turns.en: Yeah. It looks like it's the S & P 500 plus some commodities. And commodities are pretty popular for debasement, and people like commodities. Advisors are always looking to how they get commodities. The reason I say good luck with that is, A, this is expensive, 92 basis points for largely serving up things that are cheaper otherwise. The other thing is commodities tend to be bought on their own. Again, back to this idea that for most ETF advisors... who arrange portfolios, they want to pick the pieces. To quote the movie W, with Josh Brolin playing George W.
turns.zh: 对，它看起来就是 S&P 500 再加上一些大宗商品（commodities）。大宗商品在货币贬值（debasement）主题下挺受欢迎，人们也喜欢大宗商品，投资顾问们总在琢磨怎么配置大宗商品。我之所以说“祝你好运”，原因一是它贵，92 个基点，而它端上来的大部分东西本来都能更便宜地买到；原因二是，大宗商品往往是被单独买入的。这又回到那个观点：对大多数用 ETF 来搭组合的顾问来说，他们想自己去挑部件。借用电影《W》里的一句台词，那部片子是 Josh Brolin 扮演 George W.

turns.en: Bush.
turns.zh: Bush。

turns.en: I don't know what that is.
turns.zh: 我不知道那是什么。

turns.en: He said, he goes, Dick, I'm the decider. That was his quote.
turns.zh: 他说——他来了句：Dick，我才是那个拍板的人。这是他的原话。

turns.en: You should know that Eric was using his pointer finger acting while saying that. It's also currencies and fixed income, though. And I think it's systematic trend following or something like that. So is it still good luck with that?
turns.zh: 你们该知道，Eric 说这句的时候还用食指在比划着表演。不过它还包含货币和固定收益（fixed income），而且我记得是系统化趋势跟踪（systematic trend following）之类的策略。那这样它还算是“祝你好运”吗？

turns.en: Yes, absolutely. Yeah. And I understand this. It's a little bit like... you know, stacking, return stacking, and a hedge fund with your S & P. And that has been somewhat a hit, but direction is not known for this. The other thing is, generally, you know, these advisors want to be the choosers. They arrange a portfolio and they want to know what's in it. But who knows? You know, I could be wrong. This is one where I just think that... If you're wrong, we'll have them on and you can eat crow. If this gets assets, you know, I will eat crow, at least on X. If not, come back on the show. We'll talk about it.
turns.zh: 是的，绝对是。嗯，我理解这个思路。它有点像……你知道的，就是在你的 S&P 之上叠加——收益叠加（return stacking）——再加一个对冲基金。这类做法多少还算成功过，但 Direxion 并不是以这个闻名的。另外一点是，一般来说，这些顾问都想当那个亲自挑选的人，他们自己搭组合，也想清楚知道里面装了什么。不过谁知道呢？我也可能判断错。这只是我觉得……如果我错了，我们就请他们上节目，到时候你就认错吧；如果它真募到了资产，那我愿意认错，至少在 X 上认。要是没有，那就再回节目上来，我们接着聊。

turns.en: Again.
turns.zh: 再说一遍。

turns.en: If this were a company known for managed futures already, like Corey Hofstein or WisdomTree, I think I would give them maybe a little more. But it's hard to come in as a company that's known for themes and for leverage and be like, oh yeah, we're doing this complicated sort of like hedge fund-ish kind of strategy. I don't know. I looked at it and I just thought, and plus at that fee point, it just looks like a lot of beta. and only a little bit of hedge fund, and I just don't see it selling. Hard sell. Yeah, I would definitely take the under on this. All right.
turns.zh: 如果这本来就是一家以管理期货（managed futures）闻名的公司，比如 Corey Hoffstein 或者 WisdomTree，我想我可能会多给他们一点机会。但作为一家以主题和杠杆闻名的公司，硬要说“哦对，我们在做这种复杂的、有点像对冲基金的策略”，这就比较难了。我不知道。我看了看，就觉得——再加上那个费率水平——它看起来就是很多的贝塔，只有一点点对冲基金的味道，我实在看不出它卖得动。很难卖。是啊，这个我肯定押它不行。好。

turns.en: I guess you have to try.
turns.zh: 我想他们总归得试一试。

turns.en: I mean, if you're them. By the way, good luck with that.
turns.zh: 我是说，如果你是他们的话。顺便说一句，“祝你好运”。

turns.en: Good luck with that.
turns.zh: “祝你好运”。

turns.en: I don't blame anybody for trying. I mean, you have to be in it to win it.
turns.zh: 我不怪任何人去尝试。毕竟，你得先下场，才有机会赢。

turns.en: That's true. I think the tone says a lot. It's either good luck with that or good luck with that. Good luck with that. Why don't you give it a try, Eric?
turns.zh: 这倒是真的。我觉得这个语气很能说明问题——要么是那种“祝你好运”，要么是另一种“祝你好运”。“祝你好运”。Eric，你要不要也来试一句？

turns.en: Well, when we say it on the team, we mean it like good luck with that. Like, yo, dude, good luck with that. Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们团队里说这句的时候，是那种“祝你好运”的意思。就像——哟，哥们儿，祝你好运吧。对。

turns.en: Thanks for listening to Trillions. Until next time, you can find us on the Bloomberg Terminal, Bloomberg.com, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever else you like to listen. We'd love to hear from you.
turns.zh: 感谢收听 Trillions。下期再见，你可以在 Bloomberg Terminal、Bloomberg.com、Apple Podcasts、Spotify，或者任何你喜欢听的地方找到我们。我们很期待听到你的反馈。

turns.en: Hit us up.
turns.zh: 来找我们聊聊。

turns.en: Trillions is produced by Magnus Henriksen and Keshav Pandya. Amy Keene is our executive producer. Cheryl Brumley is the head of Bloomberg Podcasts.
turns.zh: Trillions 由 Magnus Henriksen 和 Keshav Pandya 制作，Amy Keene 是我们的执行制作人，Cheryl Brumley 是 Bloomberg Podcasts 的负责人。

turns.en: Bye.
turns.zh: 再见。
